profile.summary: Since 2018, ASCOM International has supplied signage media, materials, equipment and road safety solutions, and the company also works in manufacturing, technology, construction and supply.
profile.about:
Since 2018, ASCOM International has been dedicated to signage media, materials, equipment and road safety solutions. The company profile says the focus is innovation, quality and safety, and meeting a wide range of client needs.

The same profile describes a business that also trades, engineers and delivers technology-driven work. Manufacturing, construction, fire safety systems and military and defence supply are part of that range. They are parts of the company, not a single specialism.
profile.vision: To build a globally recognized enterprise that sets new standards in trading, engineering, and technology-driven solutions.
profile.mission: To empower organizations with world-class products, innovative engineering solutions, and dependable services while creating lasting value for clients, partners, and communities.
profile.head_office_address: Building # 333-B, Airline Society, Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan.
profile.factory_address: Plot # 742, 743, Sundar Industrial Estate, Wara Siddhu, Lahore, Punjab, Pakistan.
profile.hours_weekday: Monday to Saturday, 09:00 AM to 05:00 PM
profile.map_factory_note: The map marks Sundar Industrial Estate. It is not a surveyed pin for plots 742–743.
profile.seo_description: Signage, branding and visual identity from Lahore since 2018, with manufacturing, vehicles, road safety and construction.

settings.hero_text: Signage, materials, equipment and road safety since 2018, with manufacturing, technology, construction and supply as part of the same company.
settings.intro_title: A Lahore company with more than one craft.
settings.intro_body:
ASCOM has worked in signage media since 2018, and that is only one part of the company. The same business also manufactures, fits out vehicles and takes on wider project work.

The pages that follow show those areas. They are examples of the work, not a closed list of everything ASCOM can be asked to do.
settings.cta_text: Talk to the team about signage, branding, manufacturing or a construction requirement.

divisions.name: Creative Solutions
divisions.summary: Signage, brand visibility and marketing material. ASCOM has worked in signage media since 2018.
divisions.body:
Since 2018, ASCOM has described itself as a signage media company, making customised work that improves brand visibility and communication.

The creative page groups that work into trade marketing, petroleum retail, out-of-home media, road safety products, packaging, giveaways, digital services, road signs, and shop or showroom renovation. Each group is published as a list. Individual campaigns, sizes and material specifications are not published.

divisions.name: Construction
divisions.summary: Commercial, industrial and residential building work, plus infrastructure, civil engineering and turnkey delivery.
divisions.body:
The company profile describes construction as high-quality, sustainable and cost-effective building for commercial, industrial and residential projects, with a commitment to safety and timely completion.

The earlier website also names highways and motorways, flyovers and bridges, buildings, power and energy, dams and airports. A prefabricated site at Sundar Industrial Estate is a published project.

The profile prints these figures for the division: 10+ years of experience, 50+ skilled professionals, 20+ completed projects, safety as a priority, on-time delivery, and 100% quality assurance. The same figures are repeated on the technology page of the profile.

divisions.name: Manufacturing
divisions.summary: In-house metal, plastic and electrical production at Sundar Industrial Estate.
divisions.body:
ASCOM describes itself as a manufacturer, not only a trading company. The factory is at Sundar Industrial Estate, Lahore. The published account says production is controlled in-house from raw material through packaging, across metal, plastic and electrical goods.

Published capabilities are CNC machining and metal fabrication, injection molding and plastic processing, powder coating, polishing and plating, product assembly, private labelling, OEM and ODM customisation, in-house quality testing, and packaging.

The same page says the company uses energy-efficient processes, waste recycling, ethical labour standards and reduced packaging waste.

A floor area and a workforce figure appear on the previous website with a note that the area should be customised to the actual size. Those figures are withheld here until the company confirms them.

divisions.name: Technology Solutions
divisions.summary: IT equipment, consulting, cyber security, networks, software, data and support.
divisions.body:
The homepage describes this division as IT services and equipment. The technology page is more specific, and this page follows that list without adding services that are not there.

Equipment categories cover computers and workstations, servers, storage, CCTV recording, and office supplies. Service categories cover IT infrastructure, network security and IT support, including a published reference to 24/7 helpdesk support.

The page also says the company works with experienced professionals, certified experts and leading brands. It does not name the certificates or the brands, so this site does not invent them.

Storage is written on the source page as “NIAS, SAN, Harddrives, Storage Arrays”. NAS is the usual term. Confirm the spelling before treating it as a product name.

divisions.name: Road Safety
divisions.summary: Traffic products and road signs listed under Creative Solutions.
divisions.body:
Road safety is not a separate page on the current website. It is a published part of Creative Solutions, in two lists: road safety products and road signs.

Products named there are traffic cones, safety barriers, reflective tapes, road studs (cat eyes), speed breakers, convex mirrors, safety bollards and high-visibility gear.

Signs named there are regulatory signs, warning signs, directional signage, reflective sign boards, custom road signs, highway signage, and urban and industrial sign systems.

Sizes, standards and reflective grades are not published. The catalogue records the names and leaves specifications empty until the company adds them.

divisions.name: Vehicle Customisation
divisions.summary: Firefighting vehicles, trailers, vehicle bodies and livery, as published in project pages.
divisions.body:
The current website has no page titled vehicle customisation. The work is published as individual projects, and those projects are the content of this page.

They cover fire crash trucks supplied to DGP Army in a joint venture with Technofire, mobile foam units supplied to DGP Army as a subcontractor with Metron International, a 1.5-ton two-wheel water trailer of 400 gallons also linked to DGP Army and Techno Fire, firefighting cylinders, a vehicle back body for Wildlife Rangers, and painting and branding for Wildlife Rangers and for RWMC operational vehicles.

Only the water trailer has published figures. Other specifications are left blank.

divisions.name: Fire Safety
divisions.summary: Fire detection, alarm systems and firefighting equipment for commercial and industrial sites.
divisions.body:
The company profile describes fire alarm and fire safety work: early detection, control panels, manual call points, alarm sounders, installation, commissioning and maintenance.

It also lists smoke detectors, heat detectors, repeater panels, alarm accessories, fire-resistant cable and fire safety signage. The profile says this range is for commercial, industrial and institutional projects.

Separate project pages already record fire crash trucks, mobile foam units and firefighting cylinders.

resources.title: Code of conduct
resources.summary: Ethical conduct, anti-bribery rules, and how to raise a concern.
resources.body:
ASCOM International is dedicated to upholding the highest standards of ethical, moral, and legal conduct in all aspects of its business. In line with this commitment, and with the aim of transparent communication, vendors and associated individuals are encouraged to raise concerns. The company states that their identity will remain confidential and that they will be safeguarded against retaliation or discrimination for reporting issues in good faith.

Anti-bribery and anti-corruption

ASCOM states that it is committed to complying with applicable domestic and international laws, regulations, and conventions related to anti-bribery and anti-corruption. It opposes corrupt practices, including bribery intended to secure business or gain an undue advantage.

The published policy says that engaging in corruption is illegal and against ASCOM's values. Unlawful payments, including facilitation payments aimed at influencing routine actions by government officials, are denounced. The company states a zero-tolerance policy toward bribery and corruption.

No bribes — whether offered by public officials, private individuals, or third parties — are tolerated. Employees, vendors, and contractors are expected to understand that offering or providing an improper benefit to sway a decision, even if the recipient is not a government representative, may result in disciplinary action and potential criminal prosecution.

Expected behaviour

Comply with applicable laws and regulations that prohibit paying or giving anything of value, either directly or indirectly, to a government official or a family member of a government official, a private individual, or employees of companies that are wholly or partially owned by a government entity.

Ensure that interactions and transactions with government officials, or with employees of companies, are clearly and accurately recorded.

Never allow joint-venture or consortium partners, subcontractors, suppliers, agents, consultants, intermediaries, or others to make prohibited payments on ASCOM's behalf.

Seek advice in advance from the division or corporate HR department, or from the department head, before offering gifts, entertainment, other hospitality, meals, travel expenses, or charitable donations.

Report observed conduct that potentially violates anti-corruption law.

Definitions published on the current site

Bribery. A bribe is an amount of money or any favour given or promised in order to influence the judgment or conduct of a person in a position of trust. A bribe may also take the form of gifts, travel expenses, below-market loans, favours, and business or employment opportunities.

Prohibited or facilitation payments. Offering or giving improper benefits, or making payments, in order to influence the decision of the recipient.

Conflict of interest. A conflict may exist when an employee, or a member of that employee's family, is involved in an activity or has a personal interest that could impair, or appear to impair, objective and fair decisions, or that could create an incentive to act in a way that advances personal interests at the expense of ASCOM.

Raising a concern

The previous website asked for a full name, company or vendor name, phone number, email address, the concern, any evidence, and a message. Use the contact form and choose “Code of conduct”. The form opens your email program, so evidence can be attached to the email before it is sent. Nothing is stored on the website. It is not a separate anonymous hotline; the previous site did not publish one.
